objective.text: Clear the outer stretch of the old road across the cold plains and bring back usable materials and equipment

pages: Wind slips through the gap in Hearth Hall's door. Leia drags the stool toward the tower, leaving only a scrape where it stood. Once, someone could sit there and warm their hands. The warmth no longer reaches it.

The old road's cargo labels have worn smooth, yet a colossus still blocks the depths. The old world left no complete explanation, only a few things still working and the people who depend on them to survive the winter.

Mira keeps her usual shifts, with Leia learning to watch the coupling beside her. The Wanderer takes a bow to the outer road to find usable materials and equipment. On their return, a place to rest will still be waiting inside.

conversations.title: Close the Door First
pages: Mira: Wanderer, close the door. The wind's getting in. It isn't warm by the entrance anymore, so Leia moved the stool toward the tower. When the haulers come back, they need somewhere to sit.
Wanderer: I've practiced with the bow, and I know the way back to town. But what's out on that old road that makes you keep watch, shift after shift?

Mira: We have fewer old parts every day, but the machinery in the tower keeps turning. No one can explain what happened before. The colossus blocks the depths. Start outside it and bring back whatever still works.
Mira: I'll keep the fire here. You win us a little road we can walk. Check your bow before you go. We can talk about whatever you bring back, but first you have to come back yourself.

conversations.title: Where the Stool Goes
pages: Leia: I used to sit by the door and listen for footsteps on the old road. Now the wind gets here before anyone does. Even the stool we kept for tired travelers has to move inside.
Mira: We'll keep that place by the door. Come watch the coupling with me by the tower. When people return, there should be hot food, and someone ready for the next shift.
Leia: Then teach me. Wanderer, you find things worth bringing home. I'll learn to look after the people who stay. Someone will need this stool again.

town_changes.title: A Seat Moved Inward
town_changes.description: The stool moves toward the tower, while its place by the door is kept. Mira tends the hall's warmth, and Leia begins learning to watch the coupling.

objective.text: Enter the loading grounds on the old freight road and clear the next stretch of the salvage route

pages: The Wanderer returns from the outer road. This stretch can be traveled both ways again. Worn cargo labels and oversized loading grounds still trace the shape of the freight traffic that once passed through.
Taren knows the freight road farther in and wants to hear where the bow proved awkward. The next search should make the equipment more useful and the journey home less dangerous.

conversations.title: Learn the Outer Road
pages: Taren: You came back from the outer road with your bow still in hand. I used to test bows just to see if they shot straight. Now I have to ask whether one can bring you home.
Taren: Farther in are the loading grounds. You can still make out the old freight road. Don't rush the colossus. Learn this stretch first, then tell me where the bow let you down.
Wanderer: This trip showed me the old road can still be traveled. I want to find equipment that fits, then see how far this bow can take me.

town_changes.title: An Open Round Trip
town_changes.description: The outer salvage road is passable again, sparing haulers one detour. Taren can use this freight route to explain the way farther in.

objective.text: Compare the equipment you brought back and prepare for another trip deeper along the old road

pages: The equipment in the pack still carries the cold from outside. It was not on the list. The old world fell apart, but these things can still do useful work in someone's hands.
Oren's first question is what it can still do. Compare it with what you wear to see which gap it fills, or simply keep it for now. Getting home next time matters more than a promising shine.

conversations.title: Not on the List
pages: Oren: Fresh from outside? Warm your hands first. Not being on the list doesn't make it useless. The people who used it before are gone. We'll have to see what it can do in your hands.
Oren: Keep it for now and compare it with what you're wearing. Almost nothing in this town is new. I always look for the part that still works. If it helps you get home, it's worth keeping.

town_changes.title: Room in the Salvage Shed
town_changes.description: The Salvage Shed keeps space for setting finds aside and comparing them. Oren receives the old things the Wanderer brings home.

objective.text: Test the strengths of the current setup and keep searching the old road for what it lacks

pages: The first growth observation leaves a result tied to the equipment, talents, and setup used at the time. Iven keeps it like a record of road conditions, giving the next attempt something real to compare against.
Knowing what you saw tells you what to ask next. The Wanderer can carry that question back onto the road. Neither Training nor reading is a ticket required for departure.

conversations.title: Keep the Result First
pages: Iven: We've kept what you saw this time. I do the same on the old road: record the stretch beneath my feet, so next time I know whether the road changed or I strayed.
Wanderer: I'll keep the equipment and setup alongside it. If I leave with nothing but an impressive result, I won't know what to do when I meet something different.

town_changes.title: A Page at the Record Desk
town_changes.description: Iven keeps the setup and result of the first actual observation alongside reports from the old road, ready for comparison next time.

objective.text: Choose a source that addresses your equipment gaps and prepare for the road before the colossus

pages: After facing the old road's dangers, the next trip can have a clearer purpose. Drawing on his habit of testing bows, Taren helps the Wanderer match gaps in the current setup to possible sources.
Small signs beside the Contract Board list source categories, storms, collapsed passages, and ways back. Knowing where to look does not mean knowing exactly what this trip will bring.
Mira maintains the outer watch. Leia leaves a cold meal beside the station while she waits for relief. Searches on the old road and shifts in town sustain the same long winter.

conversations.title: Which Kind, Not Which Piece
pages: Taren: When I test a bow, I start with what feels worst. Try choosing equipment that way. What is this setup actually missing?
Wanderer: I want to follow the gap, not switch whenever something catches my eye. Every trip along the old road should leave something for the next one.
Taren: The Contract Board says where different kinds of old stock tend to turn up. It also marks collapses and ways back. The exact find depends on the trip, but I can spare you some blind searching.

conversations.title: The Watch Goes On
pages: Mira: Back to the old road? Your searching gives the Salvage Shed something to hope for. But we still have to keep this little warmth alive, one shift at a time.
Mira: Iven brings news, Taren helps with your bow, and Oren takes in what you find. Don't carry the whole town on your back. Walk today's stretch well.

conversations.title: A Meal by the Station
pages: Leia: I left my meal by the station. It's cold now. I used to watch the door, afraid I'd miss someone coming home. Watching the coupling has shown me how long Mira's been waiting for relief.
Leia: I can't take a whole shift alone yet, but I can pay attention for this little while. When Mira comes, I'll give her the readings, then warm up my food.

town_changes.title: Sources on the Board
town_changes.description: The Contract Board's source signs record stock categories, risks, and ways back. The watch keeps its usual shifts along the outer stretch.

objective.text: Decide which old finds to keep, reforge, or salvage before opening more of the road

pages: Beside the Tempering Anvil, things can be kept or taken apart. Oren values the work old objects can still do. Keeping, reforging, or breaking them down for materials is a decision the Wanderer must make deliberately.
Mira relieves Leia so she can warm her meal. Leia learns to explain the readings she saw and ask about what she does not understand before leaving the station.
The bow's growth methods cannot simply become a repair plan for the tower. Oren tends the outer parts he knows, while the Wanderer prepares equipment suited to the next journey.

conversations.title: Don't Salvage This Yet
pages: Oren: Don't rush to take it apart. Whole doesn't always mean useful to you, and old doesn't always mean rubbish. Plenty of things on this anvil only survived because I looked twice.
Wanderer: I'll work out which setup it fits before I keep or change it. If I take it apart, I should know what I'm losing. I can't start searching from nothing every time I come home.
Oren: Exactly. If you want to reforge it, look at what the hammer will leave you first. Keep what can travel with you. The rest can become materials and fill another gap.

conversations.title: Let the Gloves Dry
pages: Mira: Leave those wet gloves by the hearth. Don't go out wearing something frozen stiff. Take your time with the equipment. I'll watch the coupling for Leia.
Mira: She's always afraid one missed glance will cost us. What you bring back gives Oren something to repair. Covering her shift gives her time for a hot meal.

conversations.title: Ask Before You Leave
pages: Leia: Mira came to relieve me. I told her about that reading and asked about the part I wasn't sure of. Handing over isn't just saying everything's fine and walking away.
Leia: You find useful things on the old road. I'm learning to take over the work someone else leaves me. I'll warm my meal in a moment. This time I know why it's safe to leave the station.

conversations.title: The Part I Know
pages: Oren: I know the outside of that old coupling. When it wears down, I can still mend it bit by bit. Your bow's setup reminds me that old things need the right use.
Oren: But what works on a bow can't just be fitted to the tower. We haven't seen how it's connected inside. Mending the part I do know helps keep somewhere for you to return to.

town_changes.title: A Salvage Corner Takes Shape
town_changes.description: Finds awaiting salvage and their records gather beside the Tempering Anvil. Oren considers their uses; the Wanderer decides what to keep or dismantle. Leia asks her questions before handing over.

objective.text: Challenge the Threshold Colossus blocking the salvage road and adjust equipment to the bottlenecks you actually encounter

pages: Under the observed conditions, each generation of arrows outnumbers the last: exponential growth. It is the combined result of the full equipment setup, and the shared lifetime is still counting down.
Iven keeps the complete conditions alongside fragmentary old markings. This discovery gives the Wanderer more confidence for the road, but it does not explain the whole catastrophe.

Mira leaves a meal in the hall, and the tower's shifts go on as usual. Growth in battle and heat in town each depend on their own conditions. Opening the road and keeping the town still take different hands.

conversations.title: The Earlier Pieces Matter Too
pages: Iven: This time, each generation of arrows outnumbers the last. At a fork in the old road I always wish for one more way out. Your setup makes the next generation produce more on its own.
Wanderer: The equipment and setup did it together. The last piece alone isn't enough. I want to take all of it onto the road and see how much room it can open.
Iven: Keep the whole setup. I'll tell you about the dangers I can see, and you ready your bow. However great the growth, someone still has to walk the road beneath their feet.

conversations.title: A Meal in the Hall
pages: Mira: I left you a meal in the hall. They tell me you saw more and more arrows carrying on. That gives me hope too. But you don't have to wait until the whole road is open to eat something hot.
Mira: Sit awhile. You look after your bow. We'll keep taking turns at the tower, and Leia's learning. Next time you go out, there'll be people behind you keeping this warmth.

conversations.title: Leave the Gaps
pages: Iven: Only the last digit of a date remains on the old road's markings. Put beside your result, it does make you wonder: did people back then see growth like this too?
Iven: But I haven't found the missing link. We'll keep both records, gaps and all. For now, trust what you've seen with your own eyes. Don't wager your life on a guess.

town_changes.title: One More Hot Meal
town_changes.description: Mira sets aside a hot meal for the salvager. Even after seeing growth in battle, the residents keep their usual tower shifts.

objective.text: The colossus has fallen; sort the four white cores and prepare a starter proxy

pages: The Threshold Colossus has fallen. Reinforcements overlap across the gate, and no one can say what they were first meant to keep out. But now the salvage road into the depths truly is passable.
The first-kill rewards include four white cores, enough to begin proxy operation. For now, sort what was gained. The road is open, and the Wanderer still decides what comes next.

Back in the hall, wind still slips through the door. Mira keeps watch, Leia asks about this shift's readings, and the stool remains by the tower. Haulers have a shorter route, but the tower will not repair itself.

conversations.title: Beyond the Gate
pages: Taren: You made it beyond the gate? I remember all those layers of reinforcement, with the colossus still standing guard. Now it's down, we can at least stop detouring around this stretch.
Wanderer: I did. The old scars are still there. I can't explain what happened before, but the equipment I found along the way carried me through. The road really is open.
Taren: Then I'll update the source signs. One less detour means less time for the haulers in the wind. Go warm your hands. I'll write the cargo list.

conversations.title: The Road Is Open
pages: Mira: The colossus no longer guards the depths of the old road. When word reached the hall, my first thought was how much wandering in the wind it would spare the haulers.
Mira: You've won the town a way through. We have to make use of it. The coupling still needs watching, and someone will be on duty tonight. That much I can promise.
Mira: Now you're home, sit down. Someone should bring a bowl to the person who opened the road. We shouldn't ask when you're leaving again every time you come through the door.

conversations.title: Don't Dismantle It Yet
pages: Oren: The road's open, and we can reach the Winterwatch Tower's casing. That will keep me busy awhile. Finding what we can still mend beats prying every old thing apart at once.
Oren: We don't know the connections inside. Leave the tower intact for now. Keep or salvage ordinary equipment as it suits you. I'll stay at this anvil and keep the things you bring back useful.

conversations.title: Leave the Stool Here
pages: Leia: When I heard the colossus had fallen, I looked at this stool first. I used to hope someone would come back along the road. Today you really moved what was blocking it.

Leia: It's still cold by the door. The stool can stay near the tower. I'll ask Mira about this shift's readings. Opening the road is your work; making sure you can warm your hands when you return is ours too.
Leia: Next time someone comes through that door, I want to tell them where they can sit before asking what it was like outside. Now there's something I can look after too.

town_changes.title: The Salvage Road Opens
town_changes.description: The colossus no longer blocks the direct salvage route. The coupling still needs watching, and the stool stays by the tower for now.

objective.text: Arrange the slot 1 setup and complete a basic Auto assessment

pages: The four white cores gained after the colossus can support a starter proxy. Four-white-core execution uses only slot 1. The Wanderer can choose a suitable setup and complete a basic Auto assessment.
Taren hopes to reduce blind searching on repeated journeys. Oren tends the chassis, and Iven waits for actual results. Letting a proxy follow a plan still requires knowing what it can do this time.

Leia learns to compare what she sees with the previous shift's readings and call Mira when they disagree. On a journey or at a handover, taking responsibility for a stretch begins with seeing it clearly.

conversations.title: Start with What It Can Do
pages: Iven: Four white cores can get a proxy started, but the old road still has to be tested a stretch at a time. Give it a plan it can carry out now. Don't send it to explore every fork for us at once.
Wanderer: I'll arrange slot 1 and choose the basic assessment. Whether it can follow the setup I tested while opening the road still depends on this trip's actual result.

conversations.title: Following Still Means Checking
pages: Leia: You're having the proxy follow a plan. I take the previous shift's readings to the coupling. I used to worry only about remembering them wrong. Now I ask whether what's in front of me has changed.
Leia: If it doesn't match, I call Mira instead of filling in the old numbers anyway. I can take on a little work, not a whole shift yet. But I don't have to stand aside waiting to be asked.

conversations.title: Chassis and Setup
pages: Oren: I can check the chassis fittings. You decide what setup goes inside. The equipment you chose on the old road still needs more than a sturdy shell here.
Oren: Let it do the stretch it can handle first. If it saves someone one round trip, we'll have more time for the town. The frame's here. I'll watch the parts I know.

conversations.title: Choose a Short Route First
pages: Taren: When I test a new bow, the first arrow doesn't go to the farthest target. Choose a short route the proxy can handle, then see how much of your plan it actually carried out.
Taren: I want less blind wandering on future cargo runs, not another thing we have to chase around cleaning up after. The colossus is down, but we still have to learn this road.

town_changes.title: A Starter Proxy Bay
town_changes.description: Four white cores are fitted to the proxy chassis. Each resident tends the part they know, while execution planning remains with the Wanderer.

objective.text: The salvage road is open and the outer stretch is stable for now; return to the hall for a hot meal

pages: The basic Auto assessment is complete. The Salvage Shed records that this delivery can go direct. The road the colossus blocked is open, warmth along the outer stretch is stable for now, and haulers face one less journey in the wind.

The stool moves a little closer to the door, though it is still colder there than by the tower. Mira keeps watch and Leia goes to serve hot food. She has moved from waiting for footsteps to taking on a little of the work.
Iven keeps the conditions of the journey, Taren puts away the cargo list, and Oren keeps his tools ready. The tower is not fully repaired, but the salvage road connects their daily lives again.
The Wanderer has found a way to keep traveling, and a place in the hall to return to. The first chapter ends with this hot meal. Tonight, sit awhile and let people finish what they have to say.

conversations.title: Eat First
pages: Mira: The assessment's done, and the Salvage Shed can mark this delivery direct. The outer stretch is holding for now. When the haulers come home tonight, they'll have spent less time in the wind.
Mira: It's still cold by the door, and the whole tower isn't repaired. But you opened the road, and everyone took up their part. This meal feels a little more secure than it used to.
Mira: Eat first. Tonight, not every word has to become the next errand. You've come back from the cold plains. You belong at this table too.

conversations.title: A Little Closer
pages: Leia: We can move the stool a little toward the door again. It's still cold there, so here is far enough. I used to guard it while waiting for someone to return. Now I check where it's warm enough.
Leia: Mira's still at the station. I'll serve the food, then make sure I understand this shift. When it's my turn to handle what I can, everyone won't have to keep worrying for me.
Leia: You went to the old road and found things we could use. I found something I could do too. This stool isn't just for waiting anymore. Come, sit down.

conversations.title: Record This Stretch
pages: Iven: The assessment result is filed, and we know more about where the old road leads. Before, when people asked if it was passable, I could only point to a little stretch in the snow.
Iven: Now I can tell the next traveler about the part you've walked and tested. We'll leave the unknown parts blank. But this much solid news already means fewer detours.
Iven: I'll sit in the hall tonight too. The records can stay on the desk; a person needn't guard the paper forever. Someone coming home and explaining things beats a night of guessing alone.

conversations.title: Direct Delivery This Time
pages: Taren: The shed says this delivery can go direct. At last the cargo list has a shorter route. We'll still check each load, but if today's detour is gone, today's entry should say so.

Taren: I've tested plenty of bows. What I remember most is you returning with your equipment, again and again. Useful things need to stay in someone's hands to bring what works at the target onto the road.

conversations.title: Keep the Tools Ready
pages: Oren: The outer stretch is holding for now. Keep the tools ready and compare a few more shifts' readings. Old things still need tending. One night's celebration won't make them mend themselves.
Oren: I'll look at what you bring back for the uses it still has. What we find on the road and keep at the anvil gives people the confidence for another trip. Tonight, go eat.

town_changes.title: Direct Delivery This Time
town_changes.description: The Salvage Shed adds a note for this direct delivery. Heating along the outer stretch is stable for now. The stool is a little nearer the door, while tools and watchkeepers remain ready.

convergent.title: More, Then No More
journal_pages: In the first observation, arrow branches grew for a while, then dwindled and stopped. Under those conditions, this setup was convergent. The recorded result cannot be called ever-increasing growth.
Iven records where it stopped, like a break in the old road. The discovery gives the next search a question: which part of the setup could not sustain the branches that followed?
conversation_pages: Iven: There were more for a while, then it stopped. When I find a broken stretch of road, I mark where it is first. Wanting to cross doesn't make it a passage.
Wanderer: Then I know what to look for. I'll keep this setup, try some better-fitting equipment, and see whether the stopping point changes with it.
Iven: Bringing home a clear question means the trip wasn't wasted. Write down exactly where it stopped. Next time you'll know how much farther you got.

critical.title: Just Enough to Carry On
journal_pages: In the first observation, each generation just sustained the one before it, neither dwindling nor accelerating. That was the setup's critical result under those conditions, not exponential growth.
Iven keeps the conditions alongside the result. The Wanderer has seen the edge where continuation can sustain itself and can search for what is still missing on the next trip.
conversation_pages: Iven: This time it held steady. No fewer, but no more either. Like a narrow bridge on the old road: being able to stand on it doesn't mean there's room for more cargo.
Wanderer: I'll remember that edge. It's clearer than changing equipment by feel. Next time I find something, I'll see whether it lets the later generations carry a little more.

exponential.title: This Stretch Connects
journal_pages: In the first observation, each generation of arrows outnumbered the last, producing exponential growth within the shared lifetime. The result came from the full equipment, talents, and setup used at that moment.
This growth gives confidence for opening more of the road. Iven keeps the conditions. The Wanderer can take the whole method into battle, but a different field still calls for an actual result.
conversation_pages: Iven: Each generation outnumbered the last this time. The things you found along the way finally support one another in this setup. That's exponential growth you've seen with your own eyes.
Wanderer: I want to take the whole setup out again. The shared lifetime is still counting down, and enemies on the road differ. But now I know this method really did work.
Iven: Write down the conditions that made it happen. I'll keep noting the road's dangers, and you ready your bow. If each of us sees one stretch clearly, next time we do less blind wandering.
